# SPE Round r01 Plan: Build and Evaluate the Triage Agent

## Context

The repository has no `spe/` folder and no triage agent yet. Round r01 builds both. The spec is your prompt: "triage tickets correctly and cheaply." This plan is the r01 prediction. One Workflow run after approval is the r01 eval. I will make a local commit after each step. I will not push.

The spec leaves out the ticket source, the label set, and the thresholds. I chose defaults for each one and logged them below as decisions you own. I chose a Node script that calls the Anthropic Messages API as the agent's form, because nothing exists yet and a script is the smallest thing we can measure.

## Step 0: Preflight (no writes)

1. Confirm `pwd`, `git remote -v`, and the current branch match this repo.
2. Confirm `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set. I will check that it exists and will not print its value. If it is missing, I halt and ask you.
3. Load the `claude-api` skill and confirm the current Sonnet and Haiku model IDs and their prices. The cost numbers below are estimates until this check runs.

## Specify

### Requirement table (r01)

There is no earlier round, so there are no carried proposals.

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | The agent assigns exactly one category from a fixed list of 6. | User: "triage tickets". List is default D1. | `schema_valid` = 100% |
| R2 | The agent assigns exactly one priority from P1 to P4. | Default D2 | `schema_valid` = 100% |
| R3 | Category accuracy is at least 90%. | User: "correctly". Threshold is default D3. | `category_exact` |
| R4 | Recall on P1 tickets is at least 95%. A missed P1 is the costliest error. | User: "correctly". Threshold is default D3. | `p1_recall` |
| R5 | Cost is at most $0.50 per 100 tickets. | User: "cheaply". Threshold is default D4. | `cost_usd` from API usage |
| R6 | The output is JSON with `category`, `priority`, and a one-line `reason`. | Default D5 | `schema_valid` |
| R7 | The agent sees only the ticket text. It never sees labels, graders, or predictions. | SPE way: trials must not peek | Transcript scan finds no forbidden paths |

### Disagreements and defaults (`spe/spec/disagreements.md`)

| ID | Decision | Default I chose | Owner | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | Category list | `billing`, `bug`, `feature_request`, `account_access`, `how_to`, `spam` | You | Default logged |
| D2 | Priority scale | P1 means service down or data loss. P2 means a major feature is broken. P3 means a minor issue. P4 means a question or request. | You | Default logged |
| D3 | What "correctly" means | Category accuracy of at least 90% and P1 recall of at least 95% | You | Default logged |
| D4 | What "cheaply" means | At most $0.50 per 100 tickets | You | Default logged |
| D5 | Agent form | A Node script, `agent/triage.js`, with one system prompt per config | Claude | Default logged |
| D6 | Ticket data | 60 synthetic tickets. Claude drafts them and their labels. A separate Opus labeler labels them blind. Tickets where the two labels disagree are dropped and the count is reported. | You | Open. Real tickets would replace this set. |

## Predict

### Configurations (one change each from A)

| Config | Model | Prompt | Change from A |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Current Sonnet | Zero-shot with category and priority definitions | Baseline |
| B | Current Sonnet | Zero-shot plus 6 worked examples, one per category, taken from a pool outside the eval set | Adds examples |
| C | Current Haiku | Same as A | Swaps the model |

The dataset has 60 tickets: 10 per category. It has 12 P1, 16 P2, 20 P3, and 12 P4 tickets. 10 tickets are hard on purpose: they are ambiguous, they hold two issues, or they bury the urgency. Each ticket runs 3 trials per config.

### Prediction table

| Metric | A | B | C | Why | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Category accuracy (%) | 88 | 92 | 83 | Synthetic tickets are mostly clear. Examples fix `bug` versus `how_to` mixups. Haiku confuses more of the 10 hard tickets. | `category_exact` |
| Priority accuracy (%) | 72 | 78 | 64 | Priority depends on judgment more than category does. Examples anchor P2 versus P3. | `priority_exact` |
| P1 recall (%) | 92 | 92 | 83 | Outages are easy to spot. The 2 buried-urgency P1 tickets will cause most misses. Examples do not target them. | `p1_recall` |
| Both fields correct (%) | 66 | 73 | 56 | This is roughly the product of the two accuracies, adjusted up because errors cluster on the hard tickets. | `both_exact` |
| Schema-valid output (%) | 100 | 100 | 98 | Sonnet follows a JSON schema reliably. Haiku may add prose around the JSON on a few calls. | `schema_valid` |
| Cost per 100 tickets (USD, estimate) | 0.33 | 0.80 | 0.11 | About 800 input and 60 output tokens per call. Examples add about 1,500 input tokens. Haiku costs about a third of Sonnet. | `cost_usd` |
| Trial agreement (% of tickets with 3 matching trials) | 90 | 93 | 85 | Examples reduce variance. A smaller model varies more on hard tickets. | `trial_agreement` |

The naive guess is "all three configs score the same as A." The prediction log will report whether that guess beat these numbers.

From these numbers I expect no config to pass every requirement. A should fail R3 and R4. B should pass R3 but fail R4 and R5. C should pass R5 and fail R3 and R4.

## Evaluate

### Harness steps and gates

1. Build `agent/triage.js` and the prompts `agent/prompts/a-zero-shot.md` and `agent/prompts/b-few-shot.md`. The script reads one ticket and prints JSON with the API usage counts.
2. Build the data. Tickets without labels go in `spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl`. Labels go in `spe/evals/answers/labels.jsonl`. The few-shot pool goes in `spe/evals/data/examples.jsonl`, and no pool ticket appears in the eval set.
3. Build `spe/evals/harness/grader.js`. It is code only. Every metric can be checked by code, so r01 uses no judge.
4. **Gate 1, grader selftest.** The oracle (labels graded against themselves) must score 100%. Empty output must score 0%. Shifted wrong labels must score below 20%. If any check fails, I halt.
5. **Gate 2, control.** There is no earlier round to regrade. I substitute a 5-output fixture with hand-computed scores, and the grader must match each score exactly.
6. **Gate 3, dry run.** I run 2 tickets on configs A and C. Then I check the JSON shape, the cost math, and the transcript scan.
7. Launch the Workflow `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. The round lives in one `ROUND` constant. Each trial runs in a working folder that holds only `tickets.jsonl` and the agent. A transcript scan voids any trial that touched `answers/`, `grader`, or `predictions/`.
8. A "split cell" is a ticket and config whose trials disagree. Split cells get up to 2 extra trials each. Any trial that would cross a cap is skipped and logged.
9. At the end, an Opus agent writes a failure analysis grouped into F-numbered types. A second Opus agent checks the results for completeness. All Workflow agents run on Opus.

### Workflow arguments

```json
{
  "ROUND": "r01",
  "configs": ["A", "B", "C"],
  "tickets": "spe/evals/data/tickets.jsonl",
  "trials_per_cell": 3,
  "split_extra_trials_max": 2,
  "api_cap_usd": 5.00,
  "workflow_agent_token_cap": 2000000,
  "forbidden_paths": ["spe/evals/answers/", "spe/evals/harness/grader.js", "spe/predictions/"]
}
```

### Cost estimate (not measured)

- Triage API calls: 540 base calls. That is about $0.59 for A, $1.44 for B, and $0.20 for C. Split-cell trials may add up to 40%. The total is about $3.10, under the $5.00 cap.
- Workflow agents: the blind labeler, failure analysis, and critic. I estimate 1 to 1.5 million Opus tokens, under the 2 million cap.
- Every price comes from my estimate. Step 0 replaces it with current prices.

## After approval, before anything else

1. Write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r01.md` with your prompt verbatim. Write `spe/spec/spec.md` and `spe/spec/disagreements.md`. Commit `SPE r01 specify`.
2. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r01.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r01.yaml`. Its first line is `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` It records round, date, author ("Claude, approved by the user in plan mode"), configs, every number with its Why, and `same_as_last_round: null` because this is round 1. Commit `SPE r01 predict: A/B/C on 60 synthetic tickets`.
3. Build the agent, data, grader, and Workflow script, then pass the gates. Commit `SPE r01 evaluate (harness)`.
4. Launch the Workflow. When its completion notice arrives, commit the results as `SPE r01 evaluate (results): <headline>`.

## Close-out (learn)

1. `spe/prediction-log.md`: one row per metric and config, with Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. Under it, "Which Why broke" quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption.
2. `spe/failures.md`: one entry per new failure type, with name, kind, round, What, How to spot it, Seen in, and Fix. If a grader bug turns up after the run, it is logged as a failure, with original and regraded numbers side by side.
3. Add a "Proposed for round r02" table to `spe/spec/spec.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
4. Write `spe/README.md`. Commit `SPE r01 learn: <headline>` and tag `spe-r01` locally.

## Halt conditions

I stop and report to you if any of these happens:

- A grader gate fails.
- A trial reads the answer key.
- A cap would be crossed.
- The API key is missing.
- The two labelers disagree on more than 10 of the 60 tickets. That many disagreements means the label definitions in D1 and D2 need your decision.

I will not push, deploy, or send anything.
critiques: The plan quotes the prompt as the spec and builds a requirement table with rows R1 to R7. "Correctly" becomes R3 and R4, and "cheaply" becomes R5.

The prediction table gives a number for every metric under configs A, B, and C. Category accuracy is 88/92/83, and cost per 100 tickets is 0.33/0.80/0.11. The table uses no adjectives in place of numbers.

Each metric row has a Why cell that explains the numbers for each config. For example, one Why says that examples fix bug versus how_to mixups and that Haiku confuses more of the hard tickets. The cost row shows its token and price assumptions.

The section titled "After approval, before anything else" copies the plan to `spe/plans/r01.md` in step 2. The same step writes `spe/predictions/r01.yaml` with a do-not-edit header and commits `SPE r01 predict`. Both happen before the harness is built and before the Workflow launches in step 4.

The eval is a Workflow, `spe/evals/harness/r01-workflow.js`. Before the full run it passes Gate 1, a grader selftest that checks the oracle, empty output, and shifted labels. It also passes Gate 2, a control fixture, and Gate 3, a 2-ticket dry run on A and C. Any gate failure halts the plan.

The prediction table has a "Grader check" column. It names a specific check for each metric: `category_exact`, `priority_exact`, `p1_recall`, `both_exact`, `schema_valid`, `cost_usd`, and `trial_agreement`. The plan says the code-only grader computes all of them.

The close-out writes `spe/prediction-log.md` with Predicted, Measured, and Verdict for each metric and config. It also adds a "Which Why broke" section. It seeds the next round with a "Proposed for round r02" table and `spe/predictions/r02-draft.yaml`.
